subject: maths

moments.title: Guthrie's conjecture
moments.body: Guthrie, while colouring a map of English counties, conjectures four colours suffice for any planar map. He tells his brother who tells his teacher De Morgan.
moments.takeaway: A simple-looking conjecture, asked by a student colouring a map.

moments.title: Kempe's flawed proof
moments.body: Kempe publishes a proof; everyone believes it. Eleven years later Heawood finds a flaw, but salvages a five-colour theorem.
moments.takeaway: A famous false proof lasts eleven years.

moments.title: Appel-Haken computer proof
moments.body: Appel and Haken prove four colours suffice using a computer to check ~1,500 cases. Mathematicians debate whether a proof that can't be verified by hand is a proof at all.
moments.takeaway: The first major computer-assisted proof divides the community.

moments.title: Formalised in Coq
moments.body: Gonthier formalises the entire proof in the Coq proof assistant. The computer not only checks cases but verifies every logical step. The proof becomes universally accepted.
moments.takeaway: Proof assistants vindicate a 130-year-old controversial theorem.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Proof assistants (Lean, Coq, Isabelle) are increasingly used in mathematics. Major theorems (Kepler conjecture, four colour, odd-order theorem) have been formalised.
now.open_questions: Will most major theorems be machine-checked within decades?

reflection: A computer-assisted proof is opaque to humans. What does 'understanding' a proof mean?
